sentences.text: Researchers investigated whether organoid models can reproduce the dynamic changes seen in natural inner ear development by using 3D high-resolution imaging to track changes in the number, size, and shape of presynaptic ribbons as human inner ear organoids matured.

The study notes that natural hair cell development involves ribbons growing larger while their total count drops, a pattern where the number of nerve fibers touching the hair cells went down over time, which the authors interpret as a sign of refining connections.

The observed changes in the human organoids matched patterns seen in mouse hair cells, suggesting the human model mimics the assembly and refinement process, though the authors note this is a model comparison rather than a direct human result.
